page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge exhibits modest computational performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the lower performance tiers, with single-core Geekbench scores categorized as poor. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a contrast, with read-only operations performing in the bottom 25%, while large-block write operations achieve average tier performance. Cryptographic and compression tasks, including gzip and bzip3, also demonstrate weak to poor throughput.

Given its high memory density relative to processing power, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU cycles. It is suitable for hosting medium-sized in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. However, the weak CPU performance and lack of local storage make it less suitable for high-throughput database operations, intensive web serving, or complex LLM inference tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance offers a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff: while the instance provides substantial memory capacity, its CPU and memory read bandwidth benchmarks generally fall into the lower percentiles, with average performance limited to large-block memory write operations and small-model LLM inference. Consequently, the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads. It is best suited for caching layers, memory-bound enterprise applications, and moderate database hosting rather than CPU-heavy tasks or high-throughput web serving.
